draft.title: Multiplying matrices
card: The order of a matrix is its number of rows × its number of columns. A 2 × 3 matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns.
Two matrices can be multiplied only if the number of columns in the first equals the number of rows in the second. An m × n matrix times an n × p matrix gives an m × p matrix.
Each element of the answer is a row of the first matrix times a column of the second. Multiply the pairs in order, then add them.
Row [2 3] times column [4 5] (read down) = 2 × 4 + 3 × 5 = 8 + 15 = 23. This is one element of the answer.
draft.remember: Columns of the first must match rows of the second. Each element is row times column, then add.

a.q: A is a 2 × 3 matrix and B is a 3 × 4 matrix. What is the order of the product AB?
a.why: The inner numbers (3 and 3) match, so the product exists. The answer has the outer numbers: 2 rows from A and 4 columns from B. 3 × 3 is wrong because it uses the inner numbers, which are used up in the multiplying.
a.clue: Look at the outer numbers once the inner ones match.

b.q: What is the element in the first row and first column of the product of [2 3] (a row) and [4 5] (a column, read down)... use [1 2 3] times the column [4 5 6]?
b.why: Multiply the pairs and add: 1 × 4 + 2 × 5 + 3 × 6 = 4 + 10 + 18 = 32. The answer 21 comes from adding the pairs wrongly, as 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6. The answer 15 is only the sum of the second matrix.
b.clue: Multiply each pair in order, then add the results.

problems.detail: The stem is garbled. It starts asking about [2 3] times [4 5], whose answer is 23 and is not an option, then breaks off with '...' and switches to [1 2 3] times [4 5 6]. Students cannot tell which product is being asked about. The stem should ask only about [1 2 3] times the column [4 5 6].

check.summary: Question b's stem is a broken draft that mixes the card's [2 3]×[4 5] example with a new [1 2 3]×[4 5 6] product, so it needs rewriting to ask about one product only. Everything else checks out: (a) is 2 × 4 and (b) is 32.

b.q: A is the row [1 2 3] and B is the column [4 5 6], read down. AB has one element. What is it?
